title: Signals
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/0/title: Three positions relative to the cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/0/body: Ichimoku's simplest rule: price **above the cloud** means a **bullish** bias, **below the cloud** means **bearish**, and **inside the cloud** means the market is **balanced and undecided**. Many traders don't take trend trades while price is inside the cloud.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/1/title: The cloud as support and resistance
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/1/body: In an uptrend, the **top of the cloud** is the first support and the **bottom of the cloud** is deeper support. In a downtrend it's the reverse: the bottom of the cloud is the first **resistance**. A decisive close on the other side of the cloud changes the bias.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/2/prompt: According to Ichimoku, what's this chart's bias?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/2/explanati: Price is moving entirely below a red cloud. The bias is bearish, and the cloud overhead acts as resistance.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/3/prompt: Price is above a bullish cloud. Tap the candle that came back to the cloud and found support there.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/3/explanati: This candle's lower wick dipped into the top of the cloud, but it closed above the cloud. Buyers used the cloud as support, and the trend continued.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/4/statement: When price is inside the cloud, Ichimoku says the market is balanced and undecided.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/4/explanati: Inside the cloud, price is stuck between two equilibriums (Senkou A and B). Many traders wait for price to exit one side of the cloud.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/5/body: Price above a **green cloud** (A above B) paints a stronger bullish picture than price above a red cloud. Likewise, price below a **red cloud** is a firmer bearish bias. When price position and cloud color agree, that's **extra confirmation**.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/6/prompt: Price is below a red cloud and has pulled back up to the bottom of the cloud. The last candle closed below the cloud with a long upper wick. What's your call?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/6/explanati: In a downtrend, the bottom of the cloud acts as resistance. Price getting rejected from the red cloud makes a continued drop more likely. A stop loss above the cloud makes sense.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/7/prompt: Price has been above the cloud for weeks, but now a strong candle has closed inside the cloud. What's the most sensible read?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/7/options/0: The bullish bias has weakened; wait for things to clear up
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/7/options/1: The uptrend is stronger; buy more
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/7/options/2: Sell right away with a big position
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/7/options/3: Price's position relative to the cloud doesn't matter
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/7/explanati: Entering the cloud means the market has returned to balance. Until price closes below the cloud, a downtrend isn't confirmed either, so waiting makes more sense.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/8/sentence: When price is ___ the cloud, the bias is bullish and the cloud acts as ___.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l1/steps/8/explanati: Price above the cloud means a bullish bias. If price pulls back, the cloud below acts as support.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/0/body: When the **Tenkan** (fast line) crosses **above** the Kijun (slow line), it's a **bullish** signal, and when it crosses **below**, it's a **bearish** signal. It's like a moving average crossover, but built from range midpoints.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/1/title: A cross's strength depends on the cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/1/body: A bullish cross **above the cloud** counts as a **strong** signal, **inside the cloud** a **medium (neutral)** signal, and **below the cloud** a **weak** signal. For a bearish cross it's the reverse: strong below the cloud, weak above it.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/3/prompt: The Tenkan just crossed above the Kijun. Given where price is relative to the cloud, how strong is this signal?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/3/options/0: Medium, since price is inside the cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/3/options/1: Strong, since price is above the cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/3/options/2: Weak, since price is below the cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/3/explanati: Price is inside the cloud, so the bullish cross only counts as a medium (neutral) signal. Many traders wait for a close above the cloud.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/4/statement: A Tenkan/Kijun cross on its own is a completely reliable signal.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/4/explanati: Like any other signal, the TK cross gives lots of false signals, especially in a ranging market. Its strength depends on the cloud, the Chikou and price structure.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/5/prompt: On EUR/USD, the previous candle had the Tenkan at 1.0840 and the Kijun at 1.0855. Now the Tenkan is 1.0865 and the Kijun is still 1.0855. What happened?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/5/explanati: The Tenkan moved from below the Kijun to above it: a bullish cross. You judge its strength by where price is relative to the cloud.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/6/body: When price gets very **far** from the Kijun, it often comes back toward it sooner or later, since the Kijun is the **equilibrium** of the last 26 periods. That's why many traders see chasing price here as risky and wait for a **pullback** to the Tenkan or Kijun.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/7/prompt: Price is below a red cloud, a small pullback has ended, and a bearish Tenkan/Kijun cross just happened. Which direction is more likely?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/7/explanati: A bearish cross below a red cloud is the strongest kind of bearish TK cross. A continued drop is more likely. Stop loss above the Kijun or the recent pullback high.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/8/sentence: When the Tenkan crosses the Kijun heading ___, it's a bullish signal, and if it happens ___ the cloud, the signal counts as strong.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l2/steps/8/explanati: Crossing up means a bullish signal. If it happens above the cloud, it agrees with the market's overall bias and counts as strong.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/0/body: **Cloud thickness** is the distance between Senkou A and Senkou B. A **thick** cloud is **stronger** support or resistance and harder to cross; a **thin** cloud breaks more easily.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/1/body: When the **Kijun** or **Senkou B** goes flat, its range's high and low haven't changed for a while. These flat levels are market **equilibrium**, and price often returns to them or reacts at them.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/1/tip: The flat part of Senkou B in the future cloud is a level many traders keep an eye on.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/2/prompt: Price is approaching a thick red cloud from below. What's the most sensible expectation?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/2/options/1: An easy break, since the cloud is thick
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/2/options/2: A thick cloud doesn't matter at all
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/2/options/3: Price will surely cross the cloud
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/2/explanati: A thick cloud means a big gap between the two equilibriums. Crossing that whole zone is hard, so a reaction or slowdown is more likely. (Not certain, just more likely.)
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/3/prompt: Which cloud is probably easier to break?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/3/options/3: Thickness has nothing to do with breaks
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/3/explanati: Cloud 1: 1.2780 − 1.2700 = 80 pips. Cloud 2: 1.2745 − 1.2735 = 10 pips. The thinner cloud is a weaker barrier.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/4/statement: A flat Kijun means the high and low of the last 26 periods haven't changed for a while.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/4/explanati: The Kijun is the midpoint of the 26-period high and low. Until a new high or low enters the window (or an old one drops out), its value stays the same.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/5/title: Why do the lines go flat?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/5/body: Say the 26-period high is 1.0900 and the low is 1.0800. The Kijun is 1.0850, and as long as price swings between those two numbers, **the Kijun stays flat**. That's why Ichimoku lines go flat in quiet markets.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/6/prompt: Price is below a thick red cloud. Tap the candle that hit the cloud and got rejected.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/6/explanati: This candle's upper wick poked into the bottom of the cloud, but price closed below it. The thick cloud acted as resistance, and price dropped afterward.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/7/sentence: A ___ cloud usually gives stronger support and resistance than a ___ cloud.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/7/explanati: The bigger the gap between Senkou A and B, the wider the zone price has to cross, and the stronger the barrier.
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/8/prompt: Price took a sharp dive into a thick green cloud but closed above it, and the next candle was strong and bullish. Which direction is more likely?
lessons/ichimoku-u2-l3/steps/8/explanati: The thick cloud absorbed the selling pressure, and price closed back above it, so support held. A continued rise is more likely, with a stop loss below the dive's low.
